summary: A local news feature on the Annual Charity Fun Run held September 25, 2023, told through resident Ethan Jones, who went from spectator to finisher a year after a near-fatal car accident. The run drew hundreds of participants and raised money for the local children's hospital's new wing. The piece highlights community spirit, inclusivity, and resilience, ending with a town-square celebration.
one_line: Ethan Jones, recovering from a near-fatal car accident, completes the September 25, 2023 Annual Charity Fun Run supporting a children's hospital wing.
key_facts: The Annual Charity Fun Run took place on September 25, 2023, with a 7 AM start time.
Ethan Jones, a local resident, cheered from the sidelines the previous year before deciding to run this year.
Ethan suffered a near-fatal car accident a year earlier that left him with a shattered leg, and he spent months in a wheelchair.
Ethan wore bib number 1023 and ran among other first-time runners.
Mayor Patricia O'Neill opened the event with a speech saying the run is about "forging bonds, challenging ourselves, and, most importantly, raising funds for those among us who need it the most."
Money raised by the run supports the local children's hospital's new wing.
Hundreds of participants took part, and volunteers in neon vests staffed registration and water stops along the route.
By mile three the pack had thinned, with seasoned runners leading and families and walkers at the rear.
At the halfway point runners passed under a banner reading "Together We Triumph."
Ethan crossed the finish line, which was decorated with colorful banners and balloons, cheered on by the crowd.
Finishers included youths, an octogenarian jogger, parents pushing strollers, and friends arm-in-arm, reflecting the event's inclusive philosophy.
After the race the town square held live music, vendors, and children's dance-offs, and many said they would return next year.
The event's unspoken creed is "Alone, we strive; together, we thrive."
